hard_spots.why_hard: Two-paragraph incantatory list of rope arts (kakenawa, toinawa, hikinawa etc.) and holds (ganjigarame, kikkō, matsuba, rokuro-maki, takade, kote...) plus sō-returns in shin-gyō-sō variants. Tempts summarising; must be kept at full length because p164 later binds Ryūjirō 'exactly like a ganjigarame'. Requires consistent English set, not varied synonyms.

Full-paragraph kōdan explanation of hand-hauled ferry: tripods, creeper cable, iron ring, bow/stern hemp lines. Narrator pauses to savour it and adds donated retired capture-ropes from Hōzōji hemp. Do not move to footnote or compress into efficient summary.

Single-speech village rumour listing five-six dead captives with kirishitan-bateren joke and evil-eye paralysis. Delivers O-Tetsu's menace as hearsay, not fact. Keep as reported speech, not settled history.
Narrator's lecture that before telegraph/telephone/post, bad dreams and broken sandal-thongs were reason to cross provinces. Pulp sociology that licenses both escapes. Do not shrink to a sentence.

Sour-smelling cooled water and chopped surume lunch as possible poisoning. Text offers as retrospective evil surmise (邪推), never confirmed. English must keep as suspicion, not fact that O-Tetsu drugged him.

Rope biting into O-Tetsu's rich flesh as she slips free; faded red crepe loincloth against muddy water; blood-spray that is only red dragonflies. Linger at original level: neither veiled nor heated up.

Kozuka thrown 50 ken into monk's brow; Kotora's sudden side-stab of O-Tetsu, one scream, knife wiped on sleeve and returned. No remorse build-up, no confirmed death statement. Keep breath-short and deadpan.

Leap to mid-Meiji: famous First detective printed as circles ○○○○○ as Ryūjirō's later self, Kotora as dead first wife, and flat shrug whether Happō Makigumo secret was ever transmitted. Keep circles and shrug; do not explain or resolve.

narration.english_tense: Past for narrated action (de-aru / -ta habits rendered as simple past); keep present only where narrator steps forward to explain custom or mechanism in general truth
narration.frame: Third-person popular-Taishō kōdan narration in formal de-aru style with frequent stepping-forward: rumour speech, how-things-work lectures, dream sociology, half-century leap to Meiji coda. Nine titled sections (一–九) plus asterisk break and flat epilogue.

narration.tense_habits: Literary de-aru / -tari past narration with mid-paragraph gnomic asides; dreams and rumour in reported present; dialogue in period Edo speech. Do not normalise shifts or tidy chronology.

part_summaries.summary: 一: Ryūjirō readies to flee. Set-up: hatamoto swordsman on shrine-purification pilgrimage for Happō Makigumo transmission, beached three months at Awa by Living-Rope O-Tetsu, widowed oyabun with 1000 kobun and rumoured torture-murders of five-six men. Portrait of fortyish corpulent O-Tetsu; carrying on back, nursing, invisible sickness, decision to slip via back cliff to Fukuda.

二: Conscience and backstory. Training under Imahori and sole pupil of rōnin Akioka Jinpūsai; pilgrimage order to shrines. Poison suspicion (surume, sour yuhashi). Hereditary mekashi house; midnight rope-lesson catalogue (holds and shin-gyō-sō variants), mutual tying, O-Tetsu slipping bonds. Flattered as house swordsman better than Hirate Miki; thrown-rope recapture from cliff.

三: Recapture and bargaining. Hog-tied in back upstairs while O-Tetsu drinks. Ryūjirō invents/ reports nightly dream of dying kinless master; pleads one Edo nursing visit on oath to return. O-Tetsu releases and strokes rope-marks, extracts promises: foreign gunnery voyage on hoarded thousands, and jealous ban on other women. Jealousy as stored bulk.

四: Send-off and new companion. O-Tetsu kits him out (michiyuki, tsuka-bukuro, tekko-kyahan) and warns kobun everywhere. Ryūjirō hurries via Fukuda-Ichizaki toward Fūkawa-Fussa-Abiko. Meets incongruous beauty: high coiffure and heavy makeup with shabby dyed yukata and rain umbrella, bare feet. She shadows him; both claim night road for sick masters.

五: Dream essay and Kotora's tale. Narrator lectures that without telegraph/post a bad dream justified crossing provinces. Girl is Take-wari Kotora, foundling of grand-master Toradayū (now paralysed in Honjo), fleeing miserly Toramatsu from Edosaki engagement. They hurry for Hontone crossing before dark; reach lonely Shin-Tone hand-hauled ferry and begin hauling.

六: Ferry blocked. Giant fallen monk (earth-coloured nasshogi, twisted headband, sword scar) hauls opposite rope one-handed, wins tug, stern line snaps. He jeers, hides for eels. Kotora offers tightrope on creeper via umbrella; red loincloth flash, dragonflies like blood-spray, sunset double on water. Midway creeper snaps; she falls with loud splash.

七: Water rescue. Monk reappears with eel-knife, boasts he cut vine, taunts about man-eating weeds/algae. Kotora swims then is seized hand-foot-side-shoulder like living hands. Ryūjirō throws kozuka 50 ken into monk's brow, strips to tekko-kyahan and loincloth dirk, swims, finds weeds like ganjigarame, cuts free with O-Tetsu's rope-cutting method.

八: Naked robbery. Ryūjirō cuts weeds one-handed while guarding blade near Kotora, swims back to same bank. Leeches mistaken for knife wounds. Clothes, two swords, pocket things, towel and nose-paper gone. Farmhouses refuse lodging at night rule. They return to ferry under evening moon; Ryūjirō tells Kotora go on alone; she refuses, offers belly-band savings for secondhand clothes in Fūkawa.

九 + coda: O-Tetsu springs from reeds, owns theft via forward net of kobun, reveals monk as old kobun Ahodara Gonji and farmers silenced. Jealous rage beats and spits on Kotora. Ryūjirō gives up Edo trip to prove innocence; while mother-dressing him she is side-stabbed by Kotora with his dirk — one scream, woman's pride, knife wiped and returned. Asterisks: Ryūjirō as Meiji's First detective ○○○○○, Kotora dead first wife; whether secret transmitted unknown.

data.say: Rope is plot, not colour: keep catalogues full and binding-words literal; keep hero passive, O-Tetsu unglamorous-menacing, Kotora polite then abrupt, ending flat. Where passage contradicts this bible, passage wins — say so.

style_sheet.annotation_density: Sparse, for what sentence cannot give: torinawa arts, jitte / aka-fusa, Shin-Tone / Hontone geography, kirishitan-bateren joke, Mito prophecy, circles redaction. Never for what context supplies. Margin explains choices; text wins over reader ease.
style_sheet.author_voice: Brisk magazine kōdan under bookish Sinitic ornament: formal de-aru narration, performed rumour, lingering erotic-comic body description, deadpan anticlimax. Neither faux-Edo pastiche nor sleek modern flat. Keep scale comedy (carried like child, dressed after bath) and failing body (pallor, sunken eyes, grown topknot) plain.
style_sheet.honorifics_and_names: Japanese order surname-first; macrons (Ryūjirō, Jinpūsai, Toradayū). Keep Sensei for Akioka where pupil-duty weight matters; keep O- prefix (O-Tetsu, not Tetsu). 先生 addressed to Ryūjirō as 'Sensei' to keep house-swordsman irony. Danna-sama for Kotora's address. No -san/-sama beyond what English needs.
style_sheet.keep_in_japanese: Sensei, hatamoto, kobun, jitte, torinawa/kakenawa etc. with first-use gloss; place-names in romanisation (Awa, Shin-Tone, Tatsuki). Named holds in consistent English with Japanese first time (e.g. ganjigarame cross-lattice bind) then English alone.
style_sheet.quotation: Dialogue in double quotes; rumour speech and reported injunctions as quoted blocks where original sets them as performance. Keep who-said-what spare as original leaves it.
style_sheet.register: Narration literate-formal but brisk; dialogue sharply differentiated: Ryūjirō samurai-formal self-abasing, O-Tetsu cajoling-commanding-jealous, Kotora polite-feminine snapping to vulgar then flat, monk music-hall vulgar.
style_sheet.ruby_and_italics: Ruby readings (e.g. 磯貝竜次郎いそがいりゅうじろう) do not appear in English; use romanised name. Italics only for coda circles ○○○○○ and for blood-spray/dragonfly feint if needed. No italics for Japanese terms after first gloss.
